rubric_items.reasoning: pass — the stated root cause matches the cited evidence and the mechanism runs on the real code path with its callers named; I reproduced it: rounding a review id for source 'cold-test-detection-margins' at head '4c65b26cd6d9...' then appending '-figure' gives round_node_source => 'cold-test-detection-margins-4c65b26cd6d9-figure' and round_node_head_suffix => '', which is exactly the bogus source and the empty head that make the admission grant refuse both record paths; the reviewed run's own live pointer carries node.id 'cold-test-detection-margins' with head 4c65b26cd6d9..., so the corrected inverse resolves to that pointer (and to the durable row through the recovered head suffix); only recovery_review_subject.py:763 appends the suffix in non-test source, and no reader parses the id outside the two helpers.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — s17 carries one deliverable: the round node-id rule owns the rubric suffix and its inverse reads it back, so the mint and every reader agree on the reviewed run.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — the units in scope (_document, s17) declare no dependency or gate they need: s17's defect is independent of s16's host-layer declaration (the node id resolves wrongly with or without an eligible lane) and s16 is done, so no ordering edge is owed.
